note: draft geometry measured from adapter artefacts; every field carries its method; hull_rings are floor/mid/roof

methods.barrel_length: BASIS STATED: length of the adapter's recorded muzzle offset measured from the barrel mesh extremity through the parent chain, relative to the vehicle root (not a breech-to-muzzle measurement)
methods.gun_origin: global position of the GunPivot node in the adapter
methods.hull_half_width: half of the hull mesh x-extent at mid height
methods.hull_rings: y-band vertex scan of the hull mesh: [y, half-width, front z, rear z]; ring 0 = floor, 1 = mid, 2 = roof
methods.muzzle_brake: from the adapter artefact report (geometric tip check), see the note
methods.open_top: INFERRED: enclosed main battle tank, top band is closed; not a visual review
methods.ring_half: DERIVED: half of the smaller bottom-outline extent (no turret-ring node exists in this model); author may replace
methods.track_width: largest wheel mesh x-extent (the belt width across the wheel)
methods.turret_bottom: minimum y of the turret mesh vertices
methods.turret_origin: global position of the TurretPivot node in the adapter
methods.turret_outline: convex outline of the turret mesh vertices in the BOTTOM quarter (ordered, x/z)
methods.turret_taper: top-quarter half extent divided by bottom-quarter half extent
methods.turret_top: maximum y of the turret mesh vertices
methods.wheel_count: count of wheel-named meshes with x < 0 (ONE side), matching the production packets' per-side convention
methods.wheel_radius: half of the largest wheel mesh y-extent

notes: open_top is inferred, not visually verified
no separate mantlet mesh: mantlet fields left to the author
muzzle_brake is a geometric guess, not a documentary fact
